summary: Backend-only regression for KETURUNANKU new features (person_notes, family_chat, notifications, tree.note_count) + existing endpoints. All 27 pytest tests PASS (100%). Verified: RBAC enforcement (viewer 403 on POST notes/chat/files/invite), notification fan-out to editors+admins with actor excluded and viewer excluded, reply snapshot returns sender_name of original sender, /chat room_id == admin.user_id and room_name == admin.name, tree endpoint returns note_count per person and reflects newly-added notes, notifications/read?type=chat marks only chat notifications read (unread_chat -> 0). DB collections wiped post-run so first real Google user still becomes admin+root.
action_items: No backend bugs found for the new iteration. Main agent may proceed with frontend integration.

Note: /app/backend/pytest.ini forces `-n 2 --dist loadscope`. This suite intentionally shares state via a session-scoped seed fixture, so it must be run with `-n 0` (serial). All test classes were split across xdist workers by loadscope which caused double-seeding and cross-worker DB wipes when parallelized. If future agents run without `-n 0`, they will see spurious failures. Consider adding a note or a marker to run these serially.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_family_room_id() picks the first user with role='admin' via find_one without ordering — if multiple admins ever exist, room_id becomes non-deterministic. Fine today (single admin invariant) but should sort by created_at asc for stability.

add_person_note / send_chat / add_person_file all embed the actor's current name into the persisted doc; renaming a user won't update historical author_name/sender_name — acceptable but note the trade-off.
restore endpoint soft-deletes anything not in the backup payload — a partial/bad backup could nuke live data. Consider requiring a confirmation flag.
get_tree loads up to 5000 people + 10000 relations + full person_notes aggregation into a single response; fine for family-tree scale but no pagination.
get_chat loads all users into memory to enrich sender info — O(N users) per fetch; use $lookup or per-message lookup with a small LRU if user count grows.
seed_data_creation: Session-scoped fixture wipes users/people/relations/user_sessions/invites/meta/person_notes/family_chat/app_notifications, then seeds 1 admin, 2 editors, 1 viewer (each with a Bearer session token), 1 root person, and meta{root_person_id}. Teardown wipes all seeded collections. Post-run verification confirmed all collections are empty (0 docs).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run backend tests with `cd /app/backend/tests && pytest test_keturunanku_api.py -n 0 -v` — the `-n 0` is REQUIRED to disable pytest-xdist parallelism (pytest.ini forces `-n 2 --dist loadscope`). The suite uses a shared session-scoped DB seed fixture; running in parallel causes workers to wipe each other's data. Endpoints exercised: /api/auth/me, /api/tree, /api/people (CRUD + add-relative), /api/people/{id}/notes (GET+POST), /api/people/{id}/files, /api/chat (GET+POST incl. reply), /api/notifications (GET + POST /read?type=chat), /api/backup, /api/restore, /api/invite. All PASS.
